The amount of maternity leave mothers are entitled to in the U.S. depends on the legal framework and context. At the federal level, the Family and Medical Leave Act guarantees up to 12 weeks of unpaid, job-protected leave for eligible employees following childbirth or adoption [d5,d6,d7]. Federal employees covered by the Federal Employee Paid Leave Act may receive up to 12 work weeks of paid parental leave [d2]. Some states, such as New York, provide paid family leave programs that partially replace wages during leave [d6,d7]. Employer practices vary widely, with U.S. averages around 70 days and recommendations from international bodies suggesting longer durations [d4].

Because the entitlement differs by jurisdiction, employer policy, and employee coverage, there is no single national entitlement amount; instead, the leave available spans unpaid federal minimums, state paid programs, and employer-specific benefits [d5,d6,d7,d4].
